source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
Fusarium wilt of watermelon is caused by the soil-borne fungus Fusarium oxysporum (a form specific to watermelon/cucurbits). Affected plants show sudden wilting of the vine, typically starting from the growing tip and progressing down the vine; the disease often appears around the fruit-setting or fruit-development stage. When an affected stem or root is cut open, the internal vascular tissue shows brown discoloration/streaking, which is a characteristic diagnostic sign of this wilt disease.

Control measures mentioned include applying fungicides containing Benomyl or Carbendazim; when resistance is suspected or for improved effectiveness, rotating in other active ingredients such as Prochloraz and Bromuconazole is recommended. As with other soil-borne diseases, good field drainage and avoiding continuous replanting of watermelon on the same land help reduce disease pressure.
